subject: Banking
title: How M-Pesa Changed Kenya
description: One-minute skill: How M-Pesa Changed Kenya.

hook.text: M-Pesa lets Kenyans send money via text message. Launched in 2007.

buildup.text: Kenya had few bank branches but millions of mobile phones. Safaricom turned every phone into a bank account.

discovery.text: Local agents, usually small shopkeepers, handle cash deposits and withdrawals. They are the human ATM network.

twist.text: M-Pesa lifted 2% of Kenyan households out of poverty. Financial inclusion through phones changed millions of lives.

climax.text: M-Pesa proved that banking does not require banks. A phone network and trusted agents can replace entire branches.

punchline.text: No bank needed. A text message moves money across Kenya.

quiz.question: What infrastructure did M-Pesa leverage instead of bank branches?
options: Mobile phone networks and local shopkeeper agents

details.summary: M-Pesa is a mobile money service launched in Kenya in 2007 that allows users to send money, pay bills, and save using simple text messages on basic phones, bringing financial services to millions of unbanked people.
details.whyItMatters: M-Pesa proved that mobile phones could replace bank accounts for basic financial services in developing countries, creating a model that has been replicated across Africa, Asia, and beyond.
takeaways: Over 50 million people in Kenya use M-Pesa for daily transactions
It works on basic phones via SMS, not just smartphones
M-Pesa has lifted an estimated 2 percent of Kenyan households out of poverty

faq.question: How does M-Pesa work without a bank account?
faq.answer: Users register with their ID at an M-Pesa agent, typically a small shop. They deposit cash with the agent, which is converted to electronic value on their phone. Transfers happen via SMS, and recipients withdraw cash at any agent.

faq.question: Why hasn't a similar service succeeded in developed countries?
faq.answer: Developed countries already have widespread bank accounts, card infrastructure, and regulatory complexity that make mobile money less necessary. M-Pesa thrived because it filled a void where no banking infrastructure existed.
